messages:
Devon H: Quick sync — noticed inconsistent client-visible status between routing fallbacks and quota throttles. In one case the gateway returned 200 + partial output with a fallback header, console showed the route as 'Degraded', but client logs show intermittent 429s from the edge. We should choose a single client-facing contract for these cases.

Akshay: Can you paste the exact response you saw? helps to know header names + example body.

Devon H: Sure — grabbed from PROD sampling earlier: 
```http
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Redwood-Fallback: model-compat
X-Route-Reason: quota_burst
Content-Type: application/json

{ "request_id": "r_9a0", "output": "partial", "warnings": ["truncated: quota burn"] }
```

Marie: Hmm. So we have 3 signals currently: (a) HTTP status (200 vs 429/503), (b) route headers (X-Route-Reason), (c) console badge (Healthy/Degraded). Clients are reading the first and getting confused when console says Degraded. I propose we define a single client-visible surface: a new stable header `X-Client-Status: routed_degraded|throttled|ok` plus a short `client_hint` field in body when non-ok. Console maps those values to badges.

Jon P: I like standardizing the header. Slight pushback: some SDKs rely on 429 semantics to trigger retry/backoff. If we return 200 + X-Client-Status=throttled, SDKs will not back off. We either need to: (1) keep HTTP codes (429/503) when throttling, or (2) have SDKs read the new header and treat it as retry-worthy. Can't do both easily without breaking existing clients.

Akshay: Option (2) is doable if we ship a small SDK patch alongside and a console deprecation note. But that won't help users using curl or custom clients. Maybe we can emit a 429 for throttles and a 200+X-Client-Status=routed_degraded for graceful fallbacks (partial outputs). That preserves retry semantics for quota while giving a consistent routed-degraded surface for fallbacks.

Marie: Agree. So mapping proposal: 
- Quota throttles => HTTP 429 + header `X-Client-Status: throttled` + body hint "client_hint":"retry-after-seconds"
- Capacity fallback (served by cheaper/compatible model) => HTTP 200 + header `X-Client-Status: routed_degraded` + body {"partial":true, "fallback_model":"..."}
- Hard failures => 5xx + `X-Client-Status: failed`
This way console uses the header to show Degraded vs Throttled vs Failed.

Devon H: Nice. Telemetry question: what metric names and tags should we emit so ops and product can correlate? Need to be explicit for dashboards/alerts.

Jon P: Proposal: metric `client_status.events` with tag `status:(ok|throttled|routed_degraded|failed)` and `route:<route_name>` and `model_variant:<variant>`. Also emit `quota.burn_rate` and `route.fallback_rate`. Keep counts and p50/p95 latency for each status.

Akshay: Add `client_status.hinted_retries` boolean when we include a retry hint in the body. Also a `sampled_request_id` string field in logs to tie console traces to raw request.

Marie: For console UX: three badges per route (Healthy, Degraded, Throttled) with color mapping — green/yellow/orange respectively. Add hover tooltip that surfaces the canonical header and the `client_hint` message example. Also include quick links to the RFC and SDK release note.

Devon H: Rough rollout plan: 1) implement header + telemetry in gateway (can be feature-flagged), 2) update hosted SDKs to read header for retries, 3) keep 429 for quota throttles, 4) console reads header for badges. Feature-flag so we can enable per-tenant.

Jon P: Need to update our runbooks/alerts: current alert is based on 5xx and 429 spikes. We should add an alert for `route.fallback_rate` > 5% for 5m and a `client_status.events{status=routed_degraded} increase` monitor.

Akshay: Also consider adding a short `X-Redwood-Explanation` header (human-readable) for quick debugging in curl. E.g. `X-Redwood-Explanation: fallback -> model-compat due to GPU pool overflow`. That helps SREs on-call.

Marie: Good call. One more: we should be careful with PII in headers/body when exposing `fallback_model` names. Use sanitized variant tags (no customer IDs).

Devon H: I'll draft a small RFC with the header names, mapping table, metric names, rollout flags, and SDK changes. Can we aim to ship the gateway flag and telemetry in two weeks?

Akshay: Two weeks is tight but doable if we scope initial change to hosted only (no dedicated/private). We'll gate and add integration tests.

Jon P: I'll update the alerting playbook once RFC lands.

ops-bot: alert: gateway-deploy starting for feature-flag client-status-headers (deploy_id: d-9012)

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: canary deploy succeeded on us-west-2 for d-9012

Marie: Thanks — can someone own the RFC? @Devon H, assigning to you unless you want a co-author.

Devon H: I'll take it, will post draft in #eng-platform tomorrow and tag reviewers. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
